hook.spoken: Not this: replies in five places. Do this: one link.
hook.on_screen: Not this: replies in five places
hook.visual: NORAH L1-S2 over-the-shoulder, phone on a Paris café terrace; overlay = hook

voiceover: Not this: replies in five places. Do this: one link. Watch one number closely. I'll tell you which. One reply arrives by text. Another by email. A voicemail. A direct message. A comment at brunch. To know who's coming, you'd have to check all five. And you'd still wonder who you missed. Do this instead: one personal link for each guest. With Wedillybird, wedding RSVPs through the link land on one dashboard. The dashboard shows four counters: confirmed, pending, maybe and declined. Confirmed is who's coming. Declined is who isn't. Maybe means unsure. Pending means you haven't heard yet. Here's the part people skip: the date everything hangs on. Ask your caterer for the day they need final numbers. Count back from it, and leave room to follow up. Your reply-by date goes well before that day. After it, pending is your follow-up list. Next, the guest list, with a status beside every name. Follow if you want entry five of Norah's Notebook tomorrow evening. Add a guest with the form: a name, contact details, a category. And the plus-ones you allow. Each guest gets a personal link. Then export the list as a CSV file, ready for your caterer. Each row has status, plus-ones, dietary needs and notes. Now back to pending. Pending isn't a no. It's someone you haven't heard from yet. Here's the honest part: Wedillybird won't chase them for you. It shows who's pending. The nudge is still yours to send. Send it one person at a time, never in a group chat. One link per guest. One dashboard for the replies. See a sample invitation: link in bio. I'm Norah, Wedillybird's AI host. Five places, or one link. That's the whole choice.

caption:
How to track wedding RSVPs without checking five places.
One personal link per guest, one dashboard for the answers, one CSV for the caterer, and the date to count back from. Demo data on screen.
Hosted by Norah, an AI character created by the Wedillybird team.
pinned_comment: One personal link per guest, one dashboard: confirmed, pending, maybe, declined. Count back from your caterer's final-numbers date to set your reply-by date, then use the pending counter as your follow-up list. Message pending guests one person at a time, never in a group chat. The CSV export carries status, plus-ones, dietary needs and notes. Norah is AI-generated. Screens shown are real Wedillybird screens (demo data).
comment_bait: How many places are your replies in right now?

sources.fact: Work back from the caterer's headcount date and set the RSVP deadline early enough to leave time to chase
sources.title: How to Set Perfect Wedding RSVP Deadlines

sources.fact: Reply-by date set so hosts can follow up and give vendors accurate counts
sources.title: How to Word a Wedding Response Card

sources.fact: Silence does not mean no: follow up with each person individually, never a group chat or public tag
sources.title: When Should You Send a Wedding RSVP Reminder? Wording to Know

sources.fact: Check in as the cut-off approaches, keep follow-ups short, accommodate late replies where possible
sources.title: Handling your guests with grace (2008 column)

needs_proof: S06 capture should show the four counters labelled confirmed / pending / maybe / declined; S07 capture should show statuses, the add-guest form (name, contact details, category, plus-ones) and the CSV export. Every SCREEN line still works on a card if a capture is replaced.

Founder: confirm the 'Wedillybird won't chase pending guests for you' limit is still true at publication (r3 section 0 row 4: reminders go only to guests who already replied yes; the non-responder audience is switched off).
CSV content (status, plus-ones, dietary needs, notes) per r3 B1; the export also contains a guest token, so blur or crop that column on screen.
claims_review.notes: No figures are stated: 'five places' is the illustrative hook (H19), not a statistic. T30 is used as a method only (count back from the caterer's final-numbers date, leave room to follow up); the 'ten days' rule is not stated because its only source is a competitor guide and no competitor is named on screen. T31 is used for 'pending is not a no' and 'one person at a time, not a group chat'. No delivery channel is claimed; 'by text' in the opening montage describes how guests reply in the messy version, not how Wedillybird works. Wedillybird is named three times (beats 8, 25, 30).
